verdicts.reason: The dialog defines `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` while the server file exports `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.object({bookingId, guests})`; same identifier, unrelated shapes, two places to keep in sync.

`catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` never references `err`, so nothing about the failure is logged (the same shape exists in editLocation.handler.ts, but the claim is still accurate about this code).

The Attendee model has only @@index([email]) and @@index([bookingId]) — no unique constraint — and the read/filter/createMany sequence is not wrapped in a transaction, so two concurrent calls with the same address both pass the in-memory `uniqueGuests` filter.
The comment is copied verbatim from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy but MultiEmail.tsx is 96 lines and imports only @calcom/ui primitives, so the 40kb justification is untrue here.
isTeamAdmin already matches `OR: [{role: ADMIN}, {role: OWNER}]`, so `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` collapses to owner-only and locks out team admins the check was meant to allow.

`const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is a template literal, so it is never falsy; `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never fall through, and a missing code renders as the literal text `undefined:`.
The zod schema is constructed in the component body on every render although it closes over nothing; it belongs at module scope.
The change adds a tRPC handler, a dialog, a shared UI component and two email templates and contains no unit or e2e test of any kind.
Verified each detail: the three data-testid values exist and grep finds no test referencing them, and bookings-list.e2e.ts exists as an obvious home for a test.

sendAddGuestsEmails takes no eventTypeMetadata and calls neither eventTypeDisableHostEmail nor eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, unlike sendLocationChangeEmails directly above it and essentially every other sender in the file.
The ternary's else branch renders `<></>`; the two branches are `value.length` and `!value.length` and could be written as two guarded blocks with no empty fragment.

The form-builder `multiemail` factory is the same component down to the identical inputClassName string; it still carries `//TODO: Make it a ui component` and was not switched to the new packages/ui/form/MultiEmail, so two copies now exist.

Nothing clears isInvalidEmail on input change, so the red banner survives editing; the claim's aside that retrying clears it is if anything too generous — handleAdd never sets it back to false on success either.

The findFirst filters on id only and no status guard follows, while the generated ICS is hardcoded `status: "CONFIRMED"` with `method: "REQUEST"`; the list UI hides the menu for cancelled bookings but the tRPC mutation is directly callable.

`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` only flips the boolean; multiEmailValue is reset in onSuccess and in the Cancel handler but not on X/Esc/overlay dismissal, and the dialog's owner component stays mounted so the state persists.
Same finding as the other error-handling claim: the caught error object is discarded and only a constant string reaches the log.

uniqueGuests only excludes existing attendees and blacklisted addresses; the server schema has no uniqueness refinement, so a repeated address in one request reaches createMany twice (the client-side Set check is not enforced server-side).

`<li key={index}>` combined with `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)` means React keeps the same DOM inputs and shifts values into them, so focus/caret/IME state stays on the row position rather than the row content.

setIsInvalidEmail(false) appears only in the Cancel button handler; onSuccess and onOpenChange do not touch it, and AddGuestsDialog is rendered unconditionally from BookingListItem so it never unmounts.

The handler passes `guests` (raw input) rather than `uniqueGuests`, and sendAddGuestsEmails branches on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so an already-existing attendee resubmitted in the request gets the 'event scheduled' mail instead of the 'guests added' mail.

Accurate that MultiEmail imports from its own package barrel while AddressInput uses relative paths; the 'only survives because of next/dynamic' explanation is doubtful, since ~25 other files inside packages/ui import "@calcom/ui" statically and work.

The file lives in packages/ui and imports Button/EmailField/Icon/Tooltip from @calcom/ui, which now also re-exports MultiEmail — a genuine cycle, though the same pattern is already widespread in this package.
onSuccess calls setMultiEmailValue([""]) but not setIsInvalidEmail(false), so a session that failed validation then succeeded reopens with the error banner still rendered.

Initial state [""] never satisfies `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, so that early return is dead and pressing Add on an untouched dialog fails z.string().email() and shows the error banner instead of doing nothing.

eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail read metadata.disableStandardEmails and are called by every comparable sender; sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept or consult the metadata at all.

The blacklist entries are lowercased but the submitted guest address is compared raw, so `Blocked@X.com` passes; the canonical implementation lowercases the guest email and also strips plus-aliases via extractBaseEmail.

Every other booking action in this list passes seatReferenceUid for seated bookings; addGuests takes only bookingId, and since the isAttendee branch admits seat holders, any seat holder can append an attendee to the booking shared by all seats.
Same index-as-key/splice combination; correct, and the eslint preset has no rule that would have caught it.
Same finding: the schema is rebuilt per render and depends on no props or state.

eventType.disableGuests exists and drives `hidden` on the guests booking field, but the handler never reads it and the menu entry is pushed unconditionally, so the setting can be circumvented after booking.
`booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` appears twice and issues two membership queries against team id 0 for every personal booking; guarding on a present teamId would be clearer and cheaper.
`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no .max(), and every entry becomes an attendee that sendAddGuestsEmails mails with the organizer as From/replyTo.

Verified the premise: seat attendees are always created with a nested bookingSeat, capacity is counted as attendees.filter(a => !!a.bookingSeat).length, cancelAttendeeSeat resolves the attendee through seatsReferences, and get.handler filters attendees by the viewer's email when seatsShowAttendees is off — a bare Attendee row fits none of that.

Booking.responses is the source used to rehydrate a booking for reschedule/edit, and the handler writes only the attendees relation, so guests added this way are absent from responses.guests and would not survive that path.

Confirmed: the route uses authedProcedure while the sibling mutations use bookingsProcedure (organizer or collective host only), and the hand-written `isAttendee` branch grants write access — DB write, calendar update via EventManager, mail sent as the organizer — to any logged-in user whose email appears in booking.attendees.
The refine builds `new Set(emails)` from the raw strings, so User@x.com and user@x.com are two distinct members and pass the uniqueness check.

Spreading props last is the uniform, deliberate convention for every wrapper in this directory — BaseScheduledEmail is built around `props.title || default` and OrganizerRequestEmail relies on a caller-supplied title — and the two callers here pass only calEvent/attendee, so nothing can be overridden.

hideCalendarNotes only ever gates `additionalNotes`, and the CalendarEvent this PR builds sets neither field (booking.description is mapped to evt.description), so there are no hidden notes for these emails to leak.
`value = value || []` reassigns the destructured prop; the eslint preset has no no-param-reassign rule so nothing flags it, but it is a real smell carried over from the form-builder copy.
